## Q1
A term drawn from theology, concerned with the theory and method of the interpretation of human action, is known as:

## Q1 - Options
(A) Theological reasoning
(B) Philosophy
(C) Grounded theory
(D) Hermeneutics

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q14

Hermeneutics originated as the discipline of interpreting scripture and was extended to the interpretation of texts and human action generally; it is a key interpretive paradigm in qualitative research. Grounded theory is a method of building theory from data, not an interpretive tradition.

## Q3
Match List-I with List-II.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options:

| List-I (Approach of Scale Construction) | List-II (Process Followed) |
|---|---|
| A. Arbitrary approach<br>B. Factor Scales<br>C. Consensus approach<br>D. Cumulative Scales | I. A panel evaluates the items chosen for inclusion in the instrument according to their relevance<br>II. Scale is developed on an ad hoc basis<br>III. Intercorrelation of items which indicates that a common factor accounts for the relationship between items<br>IV. Chosen on the basis of their conforming to some ranking of items with ascending or descending discriminating power |

## Q3 - Options
(A) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
(C) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(D) A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q36

In the arbitrary approach the scale is built on an ad hoc basis (II). Factor scales are derived from the intercorrelation of items reflecting a common factor (III). In the consensus approach a panel judges the relevance of items for inclusion (I). Cumulative (Guttman-type) scales order items by ascending or descending discriminating power (IV) — A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

## Q5
Which of the following are methods of control of intervening variables?<br>
A. Deductive manipulation<br>
B. Inferential manipulation<br>
C. Statistical manipulation<br>
D. Physical manipulation<br>
E. Selective manipulation<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q5 - Options
(A) A, B, C only
(B) B, C, D only
(C) C, D, E only
(D) E, A, B only

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q44

Extraneous or intervening variables are controlled by physical manipulation (holding conditions constant / randomisation), selective manipulation (choosing or matching cases) and statistical manipulation (partialling out effects through analysis). 'Deductive' and 'inferential' manipulation are not recognised control techniques, so the answer is C, D, E only.

## Q6
Whether the results of a study can be generalized beyond the specific research context refers to:

## Q6 - Options
(A) Reliability
(B) Replicability
(C) Internal validity
(D) External validity

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q3

External validity concerns whether findings apply beyond the people, setting, and conditions studied. Reliability is consistency, whereas internal validity concerns causal inference within the study.

## Q7
In quantitative research strategy, the principal orientation to the role of theory in relation to research is:

## Q7 - Options
(A) Inductive
(B) Objectivism
(C) Deductive
(D) Constructionism

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q11

Quantitative research commonly begins with theory, derives hypotheses, and tests them with data. That theory-to-observation direction is deductive; induction instead builds theory from observations.

## Q8

A. It is easy to process answers.<br>
B. Respondents can answer in their own terms.<br>
C. They enhance the comparability of answers.<br>
D. They are useful for exploring new areas or areas in which the researcher has limited knowledge.

## Q8 - Options

(B) A, B and C only
(C) B, C and D only
(D) B and D only

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** D

**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q38

Open-ended questions let respondents frame answers in their own words and are useful for exploratory work. Their answers are usually harder to code and less directly comparable than standardized closed responses, leaving B and D.

## Q9
Match the sampling methods with their descriptions.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Snowball | I. Handpicked cases on the basis of specific suitability |
| B. Purposive | II. Equivalent of stratified sampling |
| C. Quota | III. Choosing the nearest individuals to serve as respondents |
| D. Convenience | IV. Identifying other respondents with the help of initial respondents |

## Q9 - Options
(A) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
(B) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
(C) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
(D) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q41

Snowball sampling obtains further respondents through initial respondents; purposive sampling selects cases for suitability; quota sampling parallels stratification; and convenience sampling chooses nearby available people. Thus A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

## Q10
Arrange the following intervals of the standard normal variate in increasing order of probabilities.<br>
A. 0 &lt;= Z &lt;= +1<br>
B. +1 &lt;= Z &lt;= +2<br>
C. +2 &lt;= Z &lt;= +3<br>
D. +3 &lt;= Z &lt; +infinity

## Q10 - Options
(A) D, C, B, A
(B) C, B, A, D
(C) B, A, C, D
(D) A, B, C, D

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q42

The standard normal density is greatest near zero and declines in the positive tail. Therefore the probability is smallest beyond +3, then from +2 to +3, then +1 to +2, and largest from 0 to +1: D, C, B, A.

## Q11
Standard deviation (S) and coefficient of variation (CV, as a percentage) are given below. Compute each mean and arrange them in ascending order.

A. S = 4, CV = 40/9<br>
B. S = 5, CV = 62.5<br>
C. S = 14, CV = 70/3<br>
D. S = 16, CV = 160/7

Choose the correct answer.

## Q11 - Options
(A) B, A, C, D
(B) C, D, B, A
(C) A, D, B, C
(D) D, B, C, A

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q6

Using CV = S/mean × 100 gives means B = 8, A = 36, C = 60, and D = 70. Their ascending order is B, A, C, D. Therefore, B, A, C, D is the correct choice. The standard deviation and coefficient of variation determine every dataset mean through the stated formula.

## Q16
The tendency of researchers to subtly and inadvertently affect participants’ behaviour, obscuring the true effect of the independent variable, is called

## Q16 - Options
(A) Response bias
(B) Experimenter bias
(C) Social desirability bias
(D) Hawthorne effect

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2025 (6 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q23

Experimenter bias occurs when an investigator’s expectations or conduct unintentionally influence participants or observations. Response and social-desirability biases arise from participants, while the Hawthorne effect is behaviour change from being observed.
